A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Marigold-DC and provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting a reliable comparison. Each contains eight main-text pages followed by references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original depth-completion evaluations, qualitative predictions, and ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–3, and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional comparator and sparse-guidance results, although some baseline scores are explicitly sourced from prior work.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the frozen Marigold backbone, DDIM/Tweedie preview, joint latent and affine-parameter optimization, min-max initialization, and median ensembling. TinyVAE is mentioned as an acceleration option; no change to the evaluated reference method is established.

E1.justification: Section 4.1 and Table 1 extend VOID evaluation from 1500-point guidance to 150- and 500-point guidance, adding sparser sensor-input conditions on the same 800 frames. The six underlying evaluation datasets, task, and synthetic pretraining sources remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the previous comparators and adds SpAgNet where results are available, DepthLab, Prompt Depth Anything, and Marigold + optim. This substantially expands comparison with foundation-model and generative approaches and adds an affine-optimization control. SpAgNet was previously cited but not evaluated in Table 1.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify 150/500-point VOID inputs and an L1+L2 scale-and-shift optimization control. Existing splits, image preprocessing, MAE/RMSE metrics, and reference inference settings remain unchanged. Table 1 also expands its stated sources for imported baseline results from VPP4DC to VPP4DC and OGNI-DC.

E4.justification: Marigold + optim adds a control testing whether optimizing scale and shift without guiding the latent representation suffices. The additional VOID densities extend quantitative evidence about sparse-guidance robustness. Existing learning-rate, denoising-step, ensemble-size, initialization, and guidance-method ablations retain their results.

E5.justification: Both versions describe ten-prediction median ensembles and median-absolute-deviation uncertainty maps in Section 3.3. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests, or independent repeated-trial statistics. The newly specified vanilla-Marigold ensemble size documents prediction configuration.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial comparator and VOID150/500 results and replaces several VOID1500 baseline scores. VPP4DC changes from 0.166/0.606 to 0.148/0.543 MAE/RMSE, overtaking unchanged Marigold-DC scores of 0.152/0.551. These are reported replacements with revised literature sourcing, not established same-setting performance gains; retained Marigold-DC results and original ablation values are unchanged.

T1.justification: The Tweedie estimate in Equation 1, affine parameterization in Equation 2, and supporting mathematical reasoning are unchanged. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: depth completion through a frozen monocular diffusion prior, test-time sparse-depth guidance, and affine anchoring without task-specific training. Claims of broad zero-shot generalization and strong benchmark performance remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly claims order-of-magnitude acceleration through TinyVAE, mixed precision, and compilation, extending discussion of computational overhead. The conclusion replaces the specific guidance-as-network-input suggestion with alternative guidance cues. Existing explanations of generalization and limitations from unrepresentative depth ranges remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly specifies ensemble size ten for vanilla Marigold, clarifies the score-guidance comparator, and names acceleration implementation options. Table 1 newly distinguishes missing code/checkpoints from checkpoints requiring retraining for zero-shot evaluation. These disclosures do not establish changes to existing experimental configurations.

R1.justification: Related work adds DepthLab, Prompt Depth Anything, concurrent test-time alignment with affine-invariant depth priors, and additional inverse-problem guidance approaches. Depth Anything V2 and TAESD are also newly cited, while BetterDepth is removed. These additions update the surrounding literature without substantially redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract and conclusion receive light rewrites, with localized clarifications and additions elsewhere and standardized bibliography wording. The section order and overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from eight to twelve method rows and six to eight benchmark-condition groups, using smaller text and revised missing-result symbols and footnotes. Tables 2–3 become more compact, and captions and text placement shift. All five figures retain their substantive visual content.

improvement.justification: The added foundation-model competitors, affine-only optimization control, and lower-density VOID evaluations strengthen the comparative evidence beyond v1's already broad evaluation. Clearer result provenance and missing-evaluation explanations improve transparency. These are useful incremental gains; the new order-of-magnitude acceleration claim lacks accompanying timing evidence.
